feed.title: The Long View

bullets: Sustainability resists the word because it hides the hard part — it is a systems problem, not a list of parts; optimizing one component in isolation pushes cost into water, land, or the grid.
The core principle is to manage the couplings, not the components — interventions must be modulated across the whole system rather than treated as discrete fixes.
Fixing emissions in isolation is a trap; the interactions between subsystems form the whole story, so risk sits inside that interconnected picture.
Risk management in this context is a discipline of portfolio-level oversight — dangerous risks get discounted when treated as separate parts rather than as coupled dynamics.
The dangerous risk is discounting — overlooking how risks compound across system boundaries, which is where the real exposure emerges.
